_comment: Tufte-Dracula palette in hex, for Mermaid only. Mermaid's color engine (khroma) throws 'Unsupported color format' on an oklch() string and aborts initialization, so no diagram in the file renders; classDef fill/stroke values choke the flowchart grammar on the literal parens in oklch(...). Every value here is therefore hex. `init` is the default (dark) palette and `initLight` is the same key set projected through the @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) palette; mermaid.js carries both and picks one at init from the --mermaid-scheme CSS token. Each hex is: the sRGB rendering of the matching tufte-dracula.css :root oklch() variable, computed through the Oklab -> linear sRGB matrix with gamut clipping (the conversion reproduces the 'was #xxxxxx' hex documented beside each oklch value in tufte-dracula.css). Edit tufte-dracula.css first, then recompute the affected hex here. mermaid.js carries these same values inline because it is inlined verbatim by consumers with no build step; contract-check.yml fails if the two disagree.

init._comment: mermaid.initialize({theme:'base', themeVariables:{darkMode:true, ...}}) in mermaid.js. darkMode has to sit inside themeVariables — mermaidAPI hands only config.themeVariables to base.getThemeVariables(), so a root-level darkMode is never seen by the theme.

initLight._comment: The same themeVariables projected through the light palette, used when :root resolves --mermaid-scheme to 'light'. mermaid.js reads that CSS token rather than matchMedia, so the forced-light sample pages pick this set up from the same cascade the rest of the sheet follows. Every 'from' names the token in the @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) :root block, falling back to the base :root where light does not override it.

initChristmas._comment: The same themeVariables projected through the Christmas dark palette, used when :root resolves --mermaid-scheme to 'christmas' (the :root[data-season="christmas"] block under @media screen and (prefers-contrast: no-preference)). Each hex is the base dark :root overlaid with that block, so a token the season block does not restate keeps its dark value. mermaid.js passes darkMode:true with this set. Every 'from' names the same token as in init.

initChristmasLight._comment: The same themeVariables projected through the Christmas light palette, used when :root resolves --mermaid-scheme to 'light-christmas' (the :root[data-season="christmas"] block under @media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: light) and (prefers-contrast: no-preference)). Each hex is the cascade a light-system reader in season gets: base dark, then the light block, then both season blocks. mermaid.js passes darkMode:false with this set. Every 'from' names the same token as in init.

classdef._comment: Node-category classDef roles for generators that emit their own 'classDef name fill:...,stroke:...' lines inside a <pre class="mermaid"> block. Not used by mermaid.js itself. Every fill draws from the --data-1..4 ramp, never from the prose accents (--pink, --green, --orange): those already carry a meaning in body copy (h1, inline code, aside bar), and the data ramp exists precisely so a diagram category cannot borrow it. stroke is --purple for every role, and color is the text that lands on the fill: --surface here, because the dark ramp is pale. THIS SET IS DARK ONLY. A page that follows the reader's appearance must not emit classDef hex at all, because a fence has no CSS to read and one hex cannot serve both palettes; emit classdefLight only on a page locked to light.

classdefLight._comment: The same four roles projected through the @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) palette, for a page locked to light the way samples/light.html is. The light ramp is mid-tone rather than pale, so the text on the fill inverts: color is --on-surface, which measures 4.98 to 5.10:1 against the four fills where --surface measures 3.45 to 3.53:1. Same role names and same 'from' tokens as classdef, resolved through the light block; palette-check.py check 2 gates both sets and fails if the role sets diverge.
